original_question: What is the physical structure of the prominence-corona transition region (PCTR), meaning the interface between the cool prominence plasma and the surrounding hot corona?
target_in_paper: Even with the new SDO observations the structure of the prominence-corona transition region (PCTR) is still unclear (Parenti et al., 2012).
correct_elements: It correctly identifies the prominence-corona transition region (PCTR) as the interface between the cool prominence plasma and the surrounding hot corona, and seeks to understand its structure.
missing_details: Explicit definition of the PCTR including its typical temperature and density ranges
Specification of which physical parameters (e.g., temperature gradient, density profile, magnetic field configuration) constitute its 'structure'
Quantification of the spatial thickness and fine-scale morphology of the PCTR
Scope of observational or modeling methods to resolve its structure
Reference to the non-LTE radiative transfer context and existing modeling frameworks
Clarification of whether the question targets static or dynamic properties
refined_question: How do the temperature and density vary across the prominence-corona transition region (PCTR), and what is the spatial thickness and fine-scale morphological structure of this interface between the cool (~10^4 K), dense prominence plasma and the hot (~10^6 K), tenuous solar corona within the framework of existing non-LTE prominence modeling?
justification: The draft captures the open problem stated in Section 1 (Parenti et al., 2012) about the unclear structure of the PCTR but lacks definitions of the region, specification of the physical parameters to be determined, spatial scales, and the modeling context of non-LTE radiative transfer. The refined question makes these details explicit and remains faithful to the paper's narrow focus.
